subject: the money and travel a long-term illness costs every month to keep getting care
citation: Goudge J, Gilson L, Russell S, Gumede T, Mills A (2009). Affordability, availability and acceptability barriers to health care for the chronically ill: longitudinal case studies from South Africa. BMC Health Services Research 9:75. doi:10.1186/1472-6963-9-75

claims.text: A chronic illness turns a per-visit price into a monthly bill: the journey and payment recur every month, repeat consultation costs can reach a large share of household income, and what must be paid today is the binding constraint, so anything requiring upfront payment or travel is read as inaccessible
evaluative_rules: Weigh care-seeking against immediate transport and out-of-pocket costs
objections: How many times a month would I have to pay this?

readings.text: Someone who sees repeated consultations reaching a large share of household income would weigh a new service by whether it removes the need to pay for each visit separately.
If what must be paid today is the binding constraint, a new service that still requires upfront payment or travel would be read as inaccessible no matter its other benefits.
Someone who has lost livelihoods and social networks would be more open to a new service only if it does not depend on having money in hand or relatives to assist.
If the cost burden fluctuates with how many times one is required to go, a new service that reduces the number of required visits would be weighed as more accessible even when monthly costs remain.

claims.text: Scarce transport funds are protected from waste: a clinic known for stock-outs is judged not worth the cost of attendance, so the patient shops around or self-treats instead
evaluative_rules: Avoid wasting scarce transport funds on a trip likely to be fruitless
objections: Do I have money for transport to get there?
Will I arrive and find the medicine is out of stock?

readings.text: Someone who has self-treated after a fruitless trip would weigh any new option by first asking whether it can be checked before spending on transport.
If a person has shopped around because of regular stock-outs, they would be more open to a new option that removes the need to travel to a clinic at all.
Someone who has judged a clinic not worth the cost of attendance would be cautious about any new option that still depends on that same clinic being stocked.
If a person has self-treated instead of consulting, they would weigh a new option mainly by whether it makes self-treatment safer or more informed.

claims.text: Unclarified referral instructions defeat unempowered patients: without asking questions, people get lost in the referral system and give up

readings.text: Someone who gets lost in the referral system and gives up would be unlikely to ask questions about a new referral process, so they would need the next steps to be made obvious without them having to ask.
If unclarified referral instructions defeat unempowered patients, a new service that relies on patients asking questions to clarify what to do next would be hard for them to weigh up at all.
Someone who is likely to get lost and give up would weigh a new policy more favourably if it removed the need to ask questions, but they might still give up if any part of it remained unclarified.

If highly vulnerable households seem less likely to take alternative action, they would be less likely to pursue a new product that requires them to take alternative action when instructions are unclear.

claims.text: Respectful, explanatory provider communication is the test of whether formal treatment is worth returning to: when it fails, families turn to prophets, traditional healers, or faith healers and abandon the health system
evaluative_rules: Judge formal treatment by whether providers give clear diagnosis, explanation, and respectful communication
objections: Will the nurses listen to me and explain what is wrong?

readings.text: Someone who has felt humiliated by nurses would weigh a new service first by whether it seems likely to repeat that humiliation, and only then by what it offers.
If a person has given up on the public health system after years of provider irritation, they would approach a new formal service expecting their continuing symptoms to be dismissed again.
Someone who left treatment because no one explained what it could achieve would look at a new service mainly for whether it promises a cure rather than just control of symptoms.
If a family has turned to a faith healer after seeing hospital treatment as a failure, they would weigh a new formal service against the explanations they already received from that healer.

claims.text: A need becomes actionable only when it can be explained and justified to others: legitimacy in the eyes of friends and relatives unlocks financial support
evaluative_rules: Support a need only when it can be explained and justified to others
objections: Can I explain this need to my family and neighbours so they will help?

readings.text: Someone who has seen a need become actionable only when it can be explained and justified to others would weigh a new offering by whether it gives them the words and standing to explain their situation to friends and relatives.
If a person has felt humiliation when unable to explain or justify a need, they would look at a new product or service for whether it spares them that exposure before others.
Someone who has seen knowledge from nurses empower a mother to become a resource would weigh a new offering by whether it passes on understanding that lets them justify needs to their community.

If a person has relied on a mother's ability to explain and justify need to unlock support, they would judge a new service by how much it strengthens the account they can give to friends and relatives.

region: Agincourt sub-district, rural Mpumalanga, South Africa
confidence: Longitudinal case studies in one rural sub-district (Agincourt, Mpumalanga): household survey of 280 households and 30 case households followed for 10 months, fieldwork 2004-2005, before the ART rollout matured. Mechanisms durable; magnitudes, prices and shares are of that time and place, not national.
